title: Differential factors and 0/4 DDT columns
summary: Clarify whether a 0/4 difference-distribution-table column is equivalent to a differential factor, distinguishing arbitrary S-box functions from permutation S-boxes.

formal_statement.body: Let $S:\mathbb F_2^4\to\mathbb F_2^4$ have differential uniformity four and let $\mu\ne0$. A nonzero $\lambda$ is a differential factor for $\mu$ if $S(x)+S(y)=\mu$ implies $S(x+\lambda)+S(y+\lambda)=\mu$ for all $x,y$. With $\operatorname{DDT}_S(a,b)=|\{x:S(x+a)+S(x)=b\}|$, determine whether this is equivalent to the $\mu$-column containing only 0 and 4.

scope.domain: Differential factors and difference distribution tables
assumptions: The source statement is read both with and without bijectivity
scope.unresolved_remainder: The general permutation theorem and higher-dimensional variants require separate verification.

progress.summary: The source work states the 0/4-column and differential-factor equivalence for a differentially 4-uniform S-box.
